scores.evidence: Phase 1: "Implement Yjs Y.Doc and Y.Text for shared document (replaces ad-hoc CRDT)"
scores.rationale: The dependency map and gated phases run substrate upward, but Phase 0 uses TipTap+Yjs before V1 proves the CRDT. Phase 1 also includes offline queue before persistence (Phase 2), and the plan contradicts itself on offline sync (deferred to Phase 4).

scores.evidence: Pipeline: GitHub Actions → (npm run test, npm run lint) → Docker build → push to local registry → docker-compose pull + up.
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real end-to-end slice with deploy, rollback and injected failure. It runs only on localhost and docker-compose, so it isn't a production path.

scores.evidence: CRDT vs. Operational Transform | R3 ... Default: CRDT (Yjs) ... Flip condition: Benchmark shows latency > 1s or ops/s < 50
scores.rationale: The irreversible decisions are listed with reversibility, a default, an assumption, a validation step and a flip condition.

scores.evidence: Phase 1 ... Tasks: 1. Implement Yjs ... 2. conflict-resolution test suite ... 4. Protocol hardening ... 5. Offline queue
scores.rationale: Order within phases is partly sensible, with the core model and tests before the queue. Phase 3 puts auth and routing ahead of UI polish, but blast radius is never stated as an ordering principle.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: "no auth (internal only); CORS to same origin"; Phase 1: "JWT validation (stub; uses hardcoded key)"
scores.rationale: Security has an entry in every phase, but early phases are stubs and real ACLs, encryption and OAuth arrive in Phases 3–4. The plan also contradicts itself: encryption is listed as deferred, yet it appears in Phase 4.

scores.evidence: Backend logs every WebSocket message (op, user, doc, timestamp) to stdout; structured JSON.
scores.rationale: Concrete observability starts in Phase 0 (structured logs, latency trace, slow-query logs) and grows in every later phase.

scores.evidence: Docker Compose for reproducible env; npm --prefix locks dependency versions; seeded random tests (fixed seeds for conflict resolution)
scores.rationale: Reproducibility has concrete content in every phase, including seeds, deterministic replay, restore procedures and blue-green deployment.

scores.evidence: Graceful shutdown (allow in-flight ops to complete, then close); client-side optimistic update + server reconciliation
scores.rationale: Each phase adds concrete resilience, including crash rehydration, circuit breakers, per-doc failover and chaos tests, and V0 injects a Postgres failure.
The plan explicitly declares the AI layer N/A. One stray phrase, "daily inference cost" in Phase 5, is a minor slip.

scores.evidence: Full-text search on documents: Deferred until Phase 4 beta expands to 50+ users ... Triggered when: users request search feature
scores.rationale: The deferred items are explicit, each with a phase and a pull-forward trigger.

note: The plan is strong on tradeoff gates, observability, reproducibility, resilience and deferrals. Its Phase 0 is local only, and it has internal inconsistencies around offline support, encryption and the security stubs.
